query: Taking nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 as the starting material, what single intervention could prevent its radiation-induced precipitation while retaining its negligible irradiation hardening and improving its suitability for practical bulk fabrication? Formulate one testable hypothesis for energetic-particle irradiation relevant to fusion service, including comparison with the unmodified alloy at approximately 8 dpa; identify the intervention and mechanism, predict quantitative or directional changes in precipitation, irradiation defects, and hardening, define the applicable irradiation and thermal boundaries, cite supporting prior evidence, and propose a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 1 at.% Ti as a solute element to nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 will reduce the precipitation of radiation-induced phases by 50%, decrease irradiation hardening by 30%, and improve thermal stability, while retaining the negligible irradiation hardening and improving suitability for practical bulk fabrication.
generation.intervention: Addition of 1 at.% Ti as a solute element
generation.conditions: Irradiation with 5 MeV Fe ions at 500°C to 10 dpa, followed by annealing at 800°C for 1 hour
generation.mechanism: Ti solute atoms occupying lattice sites and reducing the driving force for precipitation of radiation-induced phases, while also promoting defect recombination and reducing irradiation hardening
generation.predicted_outcome: Reduced precipitation of radiation-induced phases by 50%, decreased irradiation hardening by 30%, and improved thermal stability
generation.boundary: Irradiation dose up to 10 dpa, temperature range 500°C to 800°C
generation.uncertainty: The effect of Ti on the properties that must not be sacrificed, such as thermal stability or high-temperature strength, is not explicitly stated and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Irradiation of nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 with 5 MeV Fe ions at 500°C to 10 dpa, followed by annealing at 800°C for 1 hour, and comparison of the microstructure and mechanical properties with the unmodified alloy
measurements: Microstructure analysis using TEM and SEM
Mechanical property testing using nanoindentation and tensile testing
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Ti does not reduce the precipitation of radiation-induced phases or improve thermal stability, the hypothesis is falsified
